title: refactor(types): deprecate PluginComponentInput in favour of ComponentInput (stage 1 of 2)
body:
Part of #5674

> ⚠️ **Deliberately `Part of`, not the closing keyword — the dispatch asked for the closer, and this PR does not earn it.** The maintainer's ruling (2026-08-22, item 13 = A) made this a **two-stage** retirement: deprecate for a release, *then* remove. This PR is stage 1. #5674 now has an open sub-issue (#5892) carrying stage 2, so auto-closing the parent on merge would close a card with unfinished tracked work. One-word edit if the PM disagrees.

Marks `PluginComponentInput` `@deprecated` in favour of `ComponentInput`. **Nothing is removed** — the export still exists and still names the same type.

## Premise, verified before implementing

The card's rationale depends on #5671 having landed; before it, the alias pointed at a genuinely different nine-key declaration. Verified against real source, not the issue tracker alone: PR #5671 merged 2026-08-22, and `packages/types/src/plugin-scope.ts:188` on `origin/main` now reads `export type { ComponentInput } from './base.js';`. The alias is a pure alias today. **Premise holds.**

## The zero-consumer claim, measured with its scope and a control

The card is explicit that *"no importer in this repo"* and *"no importer"* are different claims, and only the second licenses deleting an export from a published package. This PR does not rely on the second — see *Why deprecate rather than delete*. The first was measured anyway, because it bounds the risk:

**Roots searched** (excluding `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.turbo/`, `.git/`): `packages/` `apps/` `content/` `docs/` `skills/` `examples/` `e2e/` `scripts/` `eslint-rules/` `public/` `.changeset/`, and the root `*.md` files (`README` `AGENTS` `ROADMAP` `CONTRIBUTING` `QUICK_REFERENCE` `CHANGELOG`). Plus the sibling `objectstack` framework checkout, and both repos' installed `node_modules`.

**Result** — `PluginComponentInput` has three occurrences repo-wide, none of them a consumer:

| location | what it is |
|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/index.ts:922` | the alias itself |
| `packages/types/src/plugin-scope.ts:177` | prose about the alias |
| `.changeset/componentinput-reexport-4972.md:10` | prose about the alias |

Framework checkout: 0. Installed packages in either repo: 0.

**Control, searched identically**, so a broken search could not read as a clean one: `AppMetadataPlugin` — a neighbour in the *same* `export type { … }` block — returns 12 hits including a real cross-package import at `packages/core/src/registry/PluginSystem.ts:10`. For the framework leg, where `AppMetadataPlugin` is legitimately absent and therefore proves nothing, the controls are `SchemaRenderer` (30 files) and `@object-ui/types` (23 files). The apparatus finds names that are there.

**The widening past code mattered.** A name with no code importers but a docs page teaching it is not a zero-consumer name. The published skills corpus and `content/docs/**` *do* teach this area — `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` documents `ComponentInput[]` and a `ComponentInput` type block, and `content/docs/guide/plugin-development.md` tells authors to declare `ComponentInput` entries. Those are precisely the pages that would teach the plugin-scoped alias if anything did. They teach `ComponentInput`. Nothing anywhere teaches `PluginComponentInput`.

## Why deprecate rather than delete

What no search from inside this repository can see is an importer on npm. That is the unmeasurable half, and it is the half that licenses deletion. The deprecation window converts a silent break into a warned one. Deprecating is undoable; deleting a published export is not — where the evidence is one-sided, the reversible step goes first. Stage 2 is tracked in #5892 and is explicitly gated on a release actually shipping this deprecation.

## Precedent followed

Not invented. This package already retires published type exports by **deprecating in place with a JSDoc tag naming the replacement**:

- [`packages/types/src/app.ts:459`](../blob/main/packages/types/src/app.ts#L459) — `MenuItem`: ``@deprecated Use `NavigationItem` instead.``
- [`packages/types/src/crud.ts:85`](../blob/main/packages/types/src/crud.ts#L85) — `ActionSchema`: ``@deprecated Use `UIActionSchema` … for new code.`` plus a removal-is-coming sentence
- [`packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts:165`](../blob/main/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts#L165) — `MenuItemSchema`: `@deprecated Use NavigationItemSchema instead.`

One deviation from `crud.ts`, deliberate: it says "removed in a future **major** version", which is wrong for this repo — objectui's own breaking changes ship as `minor` and never set `major` (they track `@objectstack`'s). The note here says `minor`.

For stage 2 the precedent set is also non-empty and is recorded on #5892: `@object-ui/data-objectstack` removed published exports twice, both as a `minor` with a **FROM → TO** breaking block and an explicit "no compile-compat stub was left" justification.

**ADR-0087 does not apply.** Its tombstones are for authorable *metadata keys* in `@objectstack/spec`, mirrored here by spec-parity tests. `PluginComponentInput` is a TypeScript type export in `@object-ui/types` — not an authorable key, not a spec symbol. `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` passes and does not match it.

## Published surface, before → after

Shown from the emitted `.d.ts`, not inferred from source.

**Before** — `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts:140`:
```ts
export type { PluginScope, PluginScopeConfig, AppPluginContext, AppMetadataPlugin, ComponentMeta as PluginComponentMeta, ComponentInput as PluginComponentInput, PluginEventHandler, } from './plugin-scope.js';
```

**After** — the same export, now carrying the tag:
```ts
export type { PluginScope, PluginScopeConfig, AppPluginContext, AppMetadataPlugin, ComponentMeta as PluginComponentMeta,
/**
 * @deprecated Use `ComponentInput` instead. Since objectui#4972 converged the
 * plugin-scoped declaration onto `base.ts`, this alias names the SAME type
 * ...
 */
ComponentInput as PluginComponentInput, PluginEventHandler, } from './plugin-scope.js';
```

That a JSDoc block on an export **specifier** survives declaration emit and lands attached to that specifier was **measured, not assumed** — a probe tag was injected, built, and located in the emitted file. It is the reason this works at all: had the tag been dropped by `tsc`, the deprecation would have existed only in source and warned nobody, and the whole window would have been cosmetic.

With comments stripped and whitespace normalised, the emitted entry point is **byte-identical** before and after (`f191480edfbb1d39` both legs) — the published *type* surface does not move, it only gains the notice. That gauge is reported with its control: renaming the alias perturbs the same hash, so it is not a gauge that cannot fail.

## Reverse verification

The diff is not a bare deletion — it adds a pin, `packages/types/src/__tests__/plugin-component-input-deprecation.test.ts`, which asserts both halves of "deprecated, **not** removed". Ablated in both directions, from a committed state:

| ablation | mutation confirmed on disk | result |
|---|---|---|
| remove **only** the `@deprecated` tag, keep the prose | deleted-text count 0, injected-text count 1, `git diff --stat` 1 insertion 1 deletion | vitest exit **1** — exactly `tags that block @deprecated` red, 1 failed / 5 passed |
| delete the alias specifier outright (stage 2 arriving early) | specifier count 0, `git diff --stat` 1 deletion | vitest exit **1** (5 failed / 1 passed); `type-check` exit **2** — `error TS2724: '"../index.js"' has no exported member named 'PluginComponentInput'` |

Both legs restored via an `EXIT INT TERM` trap, restoration confirmed by content grep and clean `git status`.

Worth stating because it is the interesting half: under the second ablation the *type-level* case **passed in vitest** (types erase at runtime) and was caught only by `type-check`. That is why the pin has both a text leg and a type leg, and why `tsconfig.test.json` being chained from this package's `type-check` script is load-bearing rather than decorative.

The pin reads **source text, not `dist/`** — same constraint `package-exports-manifest.test.ts` records: the per-PR `test` job runs with no build of the package under test ahead of it (turbo's `test` task `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, the dependency closure only), so a `dist/`-reading test would be vacuously absent-or-red on a cold cache.

## Verification

All exit codes captured **before** any pipe; verdicts quoted from what each gate printed. Union re-run against the final commit `2f7d66c2b` with a clean working tree.

| gate | exit | printed verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | ✅ 3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s) |
| `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 | ✅ No changeset declares a `major` bump. |
| `check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | 0 | ✅ All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group. |
| `check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 | ✅ OK (scanned 4902 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary) |
| `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` | 0 | ✅ 1300 files scanned against 4959 spec export names |
| `check-package-self-import.mjs` | 0 | ✅ No package names itself inside its own src/. |
| `check-published-dist-tooling.mjs` | 0 | ✅ No published package's build output carries tooling material (39 packages, 5807 tarball files) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` | 0 | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, script name echoed, no `error TS` |
| `pnpm vitest run --project unit packages/types/` | 0 | Test Files 49 passed (49) · Tests 547 passed (547) |

**Lint narrowing, declared.** Repo-wide `eslint .` was not run locally; CI runs the farm regardless. Narrowed to the three changed files, with the three pieces of evidence a narrowing needs: (1) the population came from eslint's **own** resolved config (`--print-config`), not a guess about which files count; (2) the file count came from `--format json` — 3 files, **0 errors**, 8 warnings; (3) type-aware linting is **not** enabled (`parserOptions` resolves to `{}`, no `project`/`projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. Baseline control: the same files at `origin/main` produce the **same** 8 `no-explicit-any` warnings in `plugin-scope.ts`, at line numbers offset by exactly this diff's insertions (184→193, 247→256). **Zero findings introduced.**

Also self-scanned for control bytes beyond the gate: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'` over all four changed files, no matches.

## Bump

`patch` on `@object-ui/types` — additive doc only, no type change, no removal. Stage 2's removal is the `minor`.

## Scope

Fenced to the alias line and what the precedent requires alongside it. `ComponentInput` itself is untouched; #5671's work is not folded in. One adjacent edit is included and is not drive-by: `plugin-scope.ts`'s doc block justified the re-export *because* `index.ts`' alias "keeps naming a real export" — left as-is it would tell the next reader the alias is load-bearing on the day it became deprecated. It now records the deprecation, and flags that the re-export is a **separate binding** from the file's `import type` (the import types `ComponentMeta.inputs` and stays; the re-export goes dead with the alias). The whole diff is **19 insertions, 0 deletions** across the two source files.

An adjacent zero-consumer export noticed during the search was filed as a separate card and deliberately left alone here — see #5893, where `ComponentMeta` is shown to have two published declarations already diverged by `tags`/`description`. It is *not* the same shape as this one: still a structural copy, not an alias, so it needs convergence before any retirement question applies.
